_comment: Manual corrections to the VLM scene triage (freestyle/audit.py). Model labels are never ground truth; these are the obvious errors found by eyeballing the contact sheets in data/derived/audit/ and a few frames at full resolution. Field meanings are the same as in the audit rows; 'rotated_90' is an extra field we add for frames whose scene is sideways (the VLM's upside_down means 180 degrees only). See docs/freestyle/DATA_AUDIT.md.

local/downloads/frame.jpg._why: the sharpest frame in the corpus (package README: 'lit and sharp, signage readable'); VLM said mild

island-cabinet-01/c40dc230-fc17-4edc-969._why: scene is rotated ~90 degrees (cartridge boxes lie on their side); labels still readable, so not severe

island-cabinet-01/de19c989-a538-47d7-917._why: camera upside down relative to the shelves (~180 deg): rotated 180 the two shelf boards are horizontal, the cartridge heads point up and the red Coca-Cola boxes sit on the LOWER shelf, exactly as in local/downloads/frame.jpg. The earlier 'rotated_90, shelf line runs vertically' note was wrong - that describes c40dc230/019, not this frame (near-duplicate of ab8c7fc6/043, same door angle, same flip).

island-cabinet-01/ab8c7fc6-943c-4c3d-b95._why: same ~180 deg flip as de19c989/032 (the two are near-duplicate views, pHash distance 3): VLM said upside_down=false; in the original the shelf-edge label strip sits ABOVE the cartridge row and the dark connector heads hang BELOW the brand colour, and the lower (Coca-Cola) shelf appears at the top of the frame.
